projects.title: Ka'An
projects.excerpt: A light installation inspired by Mayan cosmology, where "Ka'An" means sky or atmosphere.
projects.description:
> Ka'An is a light installation inspired by Mayan cosmology, where "Ka'An" means sky or atmosphere. The piece reflects the multi-layered structure of the Mayan sky, mirroring the building's open architecture.
Featuring 16 dynamic lights controlled by a custom TouchDesigner patch, all converging in 3D space, Ka'An creates a dreamlike atmosphere. It offers a unique experience of walking into the air, harmonised with the building's architecture and an Ableton-composed soundscape.
The site-specific work was presented during the Data Uotan festival at No Es Una Galería, Mexico City, in 2024.
projects.credits: Created by Jaco Schilp. Curated by Alejandra Metztli. Film: Mau Novelo Jarque. Presented during Data Uotan 2024, Mexico City, supported by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Mexico. Production assistance: El Destino del Arte.

projects.title: Somnia
projects.location: Le Guess Who? Utrecht · Centraal Museum Utrecht · MUTEK MX · Artweek Mexico · Inspace Mexico · Het Houtenhuis
projects.excerpt: An interdisciplinary audiovisual dance performance exploring dream states and the human body.
projects.description:
> Somnia is an interdisciplinary audiovisual dance performance collaboratively created by Mexican contemporary dancer and choreographer Alejandra Metztli and Dutch immersive digital artist Jaco Schilp. The project delves into the poetic processes within the human body and explores the dream states experienced during sleep. It presents a multidimensional approach to movement language, reflecting a non-linear and energetic interpretation of timeless realities.
> Inspired by the chemical substances secreted by the human brain, neuronal frequencies, and the subtle body connected to dream narratives, Somnia integrates these elements to craft a unique artistic expression.
The piece is a collaboration between a dancer and interactive visuals with sound, controlled by digital scanners. It is driven by the interaction between body movement and real-time processes in the computer, which together create the complete performance. The sound design for the performance was developed in collaboration with Ben Spaander (Cosmic Force) and Noah Zurhaar, adding a layered auditory dimension to the experience.
Somnia is the result of an international artistic residency, supported by the Sistema de Apoyos a la Creación y Proyectos Culturales of the Mexican government. The residency took place at Uncloud, Netherlands, in 2024.
projects.credits: Choreography & direction: Alejandra Metztli. Sound design: Ben Spaander (Cosmic Force) and Noah Zurhaar. Photography: Guillaume Versteeg.

projects.title: Points of Inaccessibility
projects.excerpt: An immersive audiovisual performance with composer Rafael Anton Irisarri: grief, loneliness and mediated intimacy rendered in point-cloud data.
projects.description:
Points of Inaccessibility is an immersive audiovisual performance by American composer Rafael Anton Irisarri and Dutch media artist Jaco Schilp, who met by chance in Mexico City in 2024.
> The title draws from the geographic idea of poles of inaccessibility, those remote coordinates on Earth farthest from any boundary or point of entry. These are not places defined by what they are, but by what they lack: proximity, reach, connection. The work reimagines this idea for our digital era, mapping emotional and perceptual landscapes that feel similarly unreachable.
> This haunting performance explores grief, loneliness, and mediated intimacy through the fragmented aesthetics of point cloud data. Shifting constellations of data points render landscapes, objects, and memories as ghostly, half-formed presences, always on the verge of dissolving. Digital spaces become both a refuge and a void, where flickering places, distorted voices, and fragile connections evoke the tension between presence and absence.
> Blending emotionally charged soundscapes with ephemeral, dissolving visuals, Points of Inaccessibility asks: in a world where our interactions are mediated by screens and signals, can we ever truly connect? Or are we just isolated points, suspended in an infinite, unreachable space?
The piece was developed during a residency at Uncloud in Utrecht in the spring of 2025, made possible through a grant from the K.F. Hein Fonds. A physical edition on BioVinyl is released by Black Knoll Editions, with worldwide distribution via Morr Music. The work has since been performed live internationally, including at Volumens Festival in Valencia.
projects.credits: Music: Rafael Anton Irisarri. Real-time point-cloud visuals & artwork: Jaco Schilp. Artwork edition: Daniel Castrejón. Vocals (closing track): Karen Vogt. Released on Black Knoll Editions. Live photography: Jota Martínez (Volumens Festival, Valencia).

projects.title: Uncloud Transliminal
projects.excerpt: Uncloud's sixth edition: a pop-up museum of multi-sensory perception inside a former forensic institute.
projects.description:
Uncloud 2021: Transliminal was a three-week pop-up museum for audiovisual art, staged in the former Pieter Baan Centrum, the Netherlands' former forensic psychiatric observation institute, in Utrecht, 30 October – 21 November 2021. More than twenty international artists pushed the boundaries between space, image and sound.
> Transliminal refers to the temporary estrangement that takes place during the intermediate phase of a transformation, of which the final destination is unknown.
> With this theme, Uncloud presents a metaphor for the current state of the world, in which we all experience estrangement from our old realities. This feeling creates a temporary reality forced on us by urgent experiences. More than ever we feel that our future is uncertain.
> In this transliminal phase, we find ourselves entangled with a process of transformation where the distinction between the tangible and intangible is undefined; where the threshold between reality and speculation is sometimes perceived as unknown. The overwhelming uncertainty of this phase is created by the in-betweenness of the state we are in. At the same time, this state leads also to renewed experience, thoughts and insights. It leads into the creation of something new: transformation.
> Within a transforming world, art can help us understand the processes we are in. By providing authentic and different experiences, art facilitates perspective, proposes possible solutions for modern challenges and composes alternative outcomes for the future.
> Transliminal art is intrinsically connected to the context in which it is made and presented. It provides a re-interpretation of not only its direct environment, but also of the world it is surrounded by. Transliminal art finds itself in the now. Based on modern knowledge and equipped with contemporary technology, it encourages a radically different and experimental approach to modern tools and narratives. It often takes the form of an abstract multi-sensory experience, where the visitor forms their own narrative, reflection and interpretation.
> Within the context of a former forensic psychiatric observation institute, Uncloud 2021: Transliminal presents the visitor a metaphor for the digitized, isolated and transitional world we currently live in, and brings this back into the tangible physical reality.
Exhibiting artists: 404.zero, Alexander Köppel, Arash Akbari, Art van Triest, Esstro9, Guenter Råler, Guillaume Versteeg, Harmke Datema-Chang, Helene Strese & Mauricio van der Maesen de Sombreff, Jaco Schilp, Jiajia Qi, Jochen Lange, Karenina van den Crommenacker, Laurie Drew, Pelle Schilling, Sébastien Robert, Siba Sahabi, Silva Westera, Silvana Hurtado Dianderas & Tomy Herseta, Studio Wae, Tatsuru Arai, TUNDRA, and Vera van de Seyp, CCU & Het Utrechts Archief.
The live programme included Robert Lippok, Arash Akbari & Farzané, Claire Rousay, Mark IJzerman & Sébastien Robert, Near Stoïc, Cinematic Laboratory, Megan Leber and Mike Lee Birds, with special events in collaboration with Modulation and Le Guess Who?.
projects.credits: A project by Uncloud (Jaco Schilp & Skander Jaïbi). Supported by Gemeente Utrecht, K.F. Hein Fonds, Mondriaan Fonds, Fonds Podiumkunsten, Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie, Prins Bernhard Cultuurfonds, W.E. Jansen Fonds and Stichting Elise Mathilde Fonds. Partners: Rijksvastgoedbedrijf, Bewaakt & Bewoond, Le Guess Who?, Creative Coding Utrecht (CCU), Sonar Traffic, Tekenen Onder Invloed, LiGHT-UP, HKU, ESWA and De Vrije Wolf.

projects.title: Jacobikerk at Le Guess Who?
projects.role: Light design, immersive projection & live operation
projects.excerpt: Turning the historic Jacobikerk into an immersive projected space for Le Guess Who? 2022.
projects.description:
For Le Guess Who? 2022 I turned the historic Jacobikerk in Utrecht into an immersive projected space for the festival's concert programme, the setting for performances by Mabe Fratti, Hatis Noit, Hinako Omori, Max Cooper and Sote & Tarik Barri.
> Working with the church's gothic architecture, light wrapped the nave and its chandeliers in slow, shifting colour, turning the building itself into an instrument of atmosphere. Through the concerts I played light and image live, letting the space breathe with each performance.
projects.credits: Light design & projection: Jaco Schilp, with Skander Jaïbi and Cris Mollee. Presented with Uncloud at Le Guess Who? 2022, Jacobikerk, Utrecht. Photography: Paulus van Dorsten.

projects.title: Uncloud × Le Guess Who?
projects.excerpt: Co-curating Uncloud's programme at Le Guess Who? 2022, with Hatis Noit, Hinako Omori, Mabe Fratti, Sote & Tarik Barri and Max Cooper.
projects.description:
For Le Guess Who? 2022 I co-curated the Uncloud programme together with Skander Jaïbi, Bob van Heur and Jacob Hagelaars. Max Cooper joined the line-up after this first announcement, playing at Ronda.
> Utrecht's contemporary and innovative art & music platform Uncloud hosted a programme during Le Guess Who? 2022 featuring Japanese artists Hatis Noit and ambient composer and sound designer Hinako Omori, as well as Mabe Fratti, a staple of the Mexican improvisation scene, and a special collaboration between Iranian electronic musician Sote and Dutch artist Tarik Barri for a mesmerizing audiovisual presentation of Sote's newest album Majestic Noise Made in Beautiful Rotten Iran.
projects.credits: Programme co-curated by Jaco Schilp, Skander Jaïbi, Bob van Heur & Jacob Hagelaars for Uncloud. Presented at Le Guess Who? 2022, Utrecht. Photography: Tim van Veen and Lisanne Lentink.

projects.title: Le Guess Who? 2019
projects.excerpt: City-wide festival projections for Le Guess Who? 2019, turning Utrecht's venues into light.
projects.description:
City-wide festival projections for Le Guess Who? 2019, the annual Utrecht festival celebrating music and the arts. Working with the LiGHT-UP collective, we wove large-scale projections into the festival's venues so that each space offered its own distinct visual experience.
> Each location was treated on its own terms, with light installations and projection mapping tailored to the interior and exterior of iconic spaces like TivoliVredenburg and club WAS. Projecting onto the architecture itself, the work infused the streets and buildings of Utrecht with a dynamic, festive atmosphere and connected the audience to the city on a visual level.
projects.credits: Projections by the LiGHT-UP collective, with decor contributions from Triomf Utrecht.

projects.title: The Anonymous Project
projects.role: Video mapping, content design & light design
projects.excerpt: A white cube on stage where artists perform in total anonymity. A special visual commission for Le Guess Who? 2023.
projects.description:
For Le Guess Who? 2023 I was commissioned to build the visual work that video-mapped the cube: a five-sided projection map driven by five projectors, with three different kinds of video content moving across its faces.
The first was a live point cloud: a real-time 3D scan of the artist inside the cube. Three depth cameras stayed in there with them and streamed the performance out through TouchDesigner, so the room could watch what was happening within without ever seeing a face.
The second was my first work with AI-generated content. I trained a model to sit across the five sides of the cube.
The third was volumetric 3D, generated in TouchDesigner from LiDAR scans of forests and places around Utrecht.
Everything was played out live from Resolume and TouchDesigner. The light design was built to make the whole room immersive, and I ran it b2b with Marc Huizinga on two light desks at the same time.
> The Anonymous Project is a stage where artists perform inside a white cube, remaining anonymous at all times: before, during and after the performance. Audiences meet the work free of reputation or expectation, focused purely on the sound.
> So the cube had to show and conceal at once. What the audience saw was the performance rendered back onto its own walls as drifting points of light. The shape of someone playing, breathing with the music, never a face. Presence without identity.
projects.credits: Commissioned by Le Guess Who? 2023. Video mapping, content design, light design & live operation: Jaco Schilp. Five-projector cube mapping; real-time point cloud from three depth cameras via TouchDesigner; custom-trained AI model; volumetric 3D from LiDAR scans around Utrecht; live playback in Resolume and TouchDesigner. Light operated b2b with Marc Huizinga on two desks. Photography: Ward Mevis.

projects.title: Rats on Rafts: Visions of Chapter 3
projects.excerpt: A one-off multidisciplinary performance bringing Rats on Rafts’ album Chapter 3 to life through video, theatre and dance.
projects.description:
> A one-off multidisciplinary performance at Le Guess Who? 2022, bringing Rotterdam band Rats on Rafts’ album “Chapter 3: The Mind Runs A Net Of Rabbit Paths” to life through video, theatre and dance.
I worked as one of the visual artists on the piece, building the projected imagery that immerses the audience in the world of Chapter 3 alongside a full creative team of decor, costume and film.
projects.credits: Visual artists: Jordi Cardenas & Jaco Schilp. Video material: A Small Production Company. Decor: Jochen Lange Studio. Clothing: Eva Arends. Photography: Tess Janssen & Jasmijn Slegh.

projects.title: Orbit 2022 Art Programme
projects.excerpt: Curating the art programme for Orbit Festival 2022 with Skander Jaïbi: SouRCe, re:gen and c55h72mgn4o5, presented by Uncloud.
projects.description:
For the 2022 edition of Orbit Festival, Skander Jaïbi and I curated the art programme for Uncloud. Three installations were brought into the festival grounds: SouRCe by Emanuel Nijkerk & Victor Dissel, re:gen by Skander Jaïbi & Cris Mollee, and c55h72mgn4o5 by Timo Hoogland.
> Rather than designing the light that year, our work was the selection and the staging, choosing works that would hold their own among the trees and the crowd, and placing each so it found its own space in the festival.
projects.credits: Curated by Jaco Schilp & Skander Jaïbi for Uncloud. Works: SouRCe by Emanuel Nijkerk & Victor Dissel; re:gen by Skander Jaïbi & Cris Mollee; c55h72mgn4o5 by Timo Hoogland. Presented at Orbit Festival 2022. Photography: Ines Kooli.

projects.title: Data Uotan
projects.location: No Es Una Galería · Art Week Mexico City
projects.excerpt: An ongoing festival and exhibition platform for art and media in Mexico City, co-founded with Alejandra Metztli.
projects.description:
Data Uotan is an ongoing festival and exhibition platform for art and media in Mexico City, which I co-founded and co-direct with Alejandra Metztli. It brings Dutch and Mexican artists together around installation, light, sound and performance, and it is the context in which my work Ka'An was first shown.
2024, Tlal-tech-utli. The first festival edition ran from 15 to 18 August at No Es Una Galería, curated by Gabriela Groso and Alejandra Metztli, and won the open call of the Dutch embassy in Mexico. The title plays the word technology against Tlaltecuhtli, the Aztec deity who gives life and death to all living things, devouring bodies and holding them so their souls can travel on to Mictlán. Through painting, sculpture, music and performance it amplified voices from both countries. The programme included Shapes by Gabriela Groso, Alejandra Metztli and Yara Saïd, Sonic Reveries: A Temporal Collage by Noise Diva, and The Absence of Metamorphosis by Lisette Ros.
2026, Art Week. In February Data Uotan returned for Mexico City Art Week at Apricot on Álvaro Obregón, curated by Alejandra Metztli, with work by Santiago Pani, Gabriela Groso, Jimena Ramos, Ricardo Saga, Harmke Datema Chang, J. Rivas, Aycanija, 11v151131_m06 and me.
> Mexico City has become a second home for my practice: every return brings a new rhythm, a new kind of chaos, and a deep connection with its artistic community.
projects.credits: Data Uotan, co-founded and co-directed by Jaco Schilp and Alejandra Metztli. 2024 edition at No Es Una Galería, Mexico City, curated by Gabriela Groso and Alejandra Metztli, supported by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Mexico. 2026 Art Week edition at Apricot, Mexico City, curated by Alejandra Metztli.

projects.title: MoMentNu
projects.excerpt: Video and projections for MoMentNu, an immersive light installation with artist Willem Geerts.
projects.description:
MoMentNu is an installation at Museum Jan Cunen in Oss, based on a concept by artist Willem Geerts. The imagery came from aerial LiDAR point clouds of the city of Oss, which I rendered in Cinema 4D. It is part of the long-running point-cloud research that also carries Panorama Utrecht, LiDAR Utrecht and Points of Light: scanning a place, then finding out what it becomes once it is only data and light. Horizontal bands of moving light are wrapped around the wooden beams and pillars of the space, turning the architecture itself into a slow, drifting landscape of projected image.
> Visitors move through the darkened room as the projections shift around them, blurring the line between the building and the picture. A quiet, immersive meditation on the present moment.
projects.credits: Concept: Willem Geerts. Realisation, video & projections: Jaco Schilp / Studio Schilp. Content built from aerial LiDAR point-cloud data of Oss, rendered in Cinema 4D. Presented at Museum Jan Cunen, Oss.

projects.title: Panorama Utrecht
projects.excerpt: A light sculpture of Utrecht built from 1.1 billion LiDAR data points, on the Stationsplein for the city's 900th anniversary.
projects.description:
Panorama Utrecht stood on the Stationsplein at Utrecht Centraal in 2022, as part of the city's 900th anniversary. The sculpture was shown again at Uncloud in 2023 and is still travelling. It is looking for a permanent location.
The composition of points is an artistic interpretation of aerial LiDAR data of Utrecht. For every point, a laser was fired at the city from a scanner in the air, and the height of that measuring point was derived from how long the reflection took. The 3D measurement of Utrecht holds roughly 1.1 billion points and comes from the Actueel Hoogtebestand Nederland dataset.
The audio composition is built from field recordings collected by cycling and walking through the city, switching between recognisable daily city sounds and composed ones. The contrast between them stands for the warm home feeling of Utrecht and the fast modern transformation of the city.
> The light sculpture Panorama Utrecht shows the city from a digital perspective: a panoramic view of small luminous points that make all the walls disappear.
> Aerial scanners fly over the Netherlands to collect billions of height data points. This work stands at the focal point between that digital world and the tangible city. A 360-degree sculpture you step into, where a play of light and a composition of city sounds together open a new perspective. You look straight through the walls of Utrecht.
projects.credits: Design & creation: Jaco Schilp. Artistic concept: Jaco Schilp and Skander Jaïbi. Audio composition: Allert Aalders and Skander Jaïbi. Construction: Sander Grooten, Edwin Schulte, Jaco Schilp, Silvana Hurtd. Technical support: Tjarco van Heese, Cris Mollee, Jelle Grutterink. Conceptual support: Skander Jaïbi, Jasper van den Dobbelsteen. Technical advice & production: Miniprinten, Luxalight, WSV Kunstoffen, DoorDouwe. With the help of Silvana Hurtd, Monique Jansen, Bas van Dolderen, Douwe Hibma, Marc Huizinga, Gerrit Schilp, Tine Liephout, Frances Rompas, Jan Willem Campmans and Juliette Osse. With thanks to Alan Grommers, Tessa van Beekhuizen, Antoon Hardeman and Nick Oomen. Presented again at Uncloud, 2023. Made possible by Stichting Uncloud, Gemeente Utrecht, Ondernemersfonds Utrecht, Klépierre, Winkeliersvereniging and Hoog Catharijne. Photography: Paulus van Dorsten.

projects.title: LiDAR Utrecht 60×60, first series
projects.excerpt: The first LiDAR Utrecht series, 60 by 60 cm, made and shown before the 30×30 physical NFTs.
projects.description: The first of the two LiDAR Utrecht series, at 60 by 60 cm. It was made and presented before the 30×30 physical NFT series.

projects.title: LiDAR Utrecht, physical NFT series
projects.location: Creative Coding Utrecht · NAR Café der Kunsten, Utrecht
projects.excerpt: A series of light sculptures that translate raw LiDAR point clouds of Utrecht landmarks into laser-cut, backlit wood.
projects.description:
> On the interface between the physical world and cyberspace, I make art that brings the two universes together. The LiDAR series interprets raw aerial LiDAR data of Utrecht into physical objects: point clouds of the city's landmarks engraved by laser into wood and lit from within by LED, framed in aluminium.
This is the second of the two LiDAR Utrecht series, following the earlier works at 60 by 60 cm. Each piece is 300×300mm and captures a single Utrecht location from a chosen perspective in 3D space. Up close the buildings dissolve into thousands of luminous points, and every wall becomes light. The first five works in the series are Tivoli Vredenburg (5.1), the Stadskantoor (5.2), the Neude library (5.3), the windmill on the Adelaarstraat (5.4), and the Nijverheid / Havenloods (5.6).
Presented as “physical NFTs”, each sculpture is paired with a digital token that registers it, exploring the boundary between digital and physical art, and the shifting role of accessibility and ownership in a digitalising world.
The series was first shown in Math Expressionism, an exhibition of work by the international community of creative coders, presented by Creative Coding Utrecht at NAR Café der Kunsten. Alongside the work the programme ran workshops and discussions on NFTs, where makers shared their experience of communities like Hic et Nunc and Artblocks, and the controversies around them.
projects.credits: Physical NFT series. Laser-cut wood, engraved LiDAR point cloud, LED light, aluminium frame, 300×300mm. Point clouds derived from aerial LiDAR data of Utrecht. Shown in Math Expressionism by Creative Coding Utrecht, at NAR Café der Kunsten in Utrecht, made possible with the support of the Creative Industries Fund NL, Gemeente Utrecht and TheElephantNL.

projects.title: Aquí y Ahora
projects.excerpt: A month in the Mexican desert, scanning nopal, agave and maguey and cutting the point clouds into wood, plexiglas and metal.
projects.description:
A month long residency at Arthouse Pani in Tequisquiapan, with twelve artists from around the world, curated by Santiago Pani. The show that closed it was called Aquí y Ahora.
I scanned the plants of the high desert around the house and turned the point clouds into physical work. One series is laser cut into white painted wood and into black plexiglas, each piece set in a frame with a light behind it, so the cloud reads as depth rather than as a picture. A second series is acid etched into brass, aluminium and copper, and every bath in the acid was printed onto paper before the next one went in, so the plate and its own history hang side by side. Titles follow the plants: Nopal, Agave, Maguey, Suculenta.
Espíritu de Nopal, a laser engraved oil painting on panel of 150 by 120 cm, was made together with Daniel Martin.
> The point cloud is a way of holding a thing as measurement rather than as image. In Mexico the subject changed and the method held. A nopal scanned at close range is a dense, bristling mass of coordinates, and cutting that mass into brass or into wood makes it a body again, something with an edge and a weight and a shadow. The acid does the last part of the work on its own, and I stopped it when it had said enough.
projects.credits: Laser cut and acid etched point cloud works: Jaco Schilp. Espíritu de Nopal made with Daniel Martin. Residency and exhibition at Arthouse Pani, Tequisquiapan, curated by Santiago Pani, 2024.

projects.title: flip-mode
projects.excerpt: An interactive light work made with Tijmen Lohmeijer and Merijn Hos, playing with perception and the acceleration of time.
projects.description:
flip-mode was commissioned by Stranded FM and Uncloud for Utrecht 900, and came out of a residency at Uncloud. It was presented at TivoliVredenburg and at Orbit Festival.
> flip-mode is an interactive light work by Jaco Schilp, Tijmen Lohmeijer and Merijn Hos which plays with our perception and the acceleration of time. Not only in terms of day and night, but also in terms of impact on our feelings and emotions.
> The endless flipping of the shades refers to the repetitive mechanical sounds of nightlife in which time seems to both slow down and accelerate, and maybe even ceases to exist.
projects.credits: An interactive light work by Jaco Schilp, Tijmen Lohmeijer and Merijn Hos. Commissioned by Stranded FM and Uncloud for Utrecht 900. Presented at TivoliVredenburg and Orbit Festival. Photography: Juri Hiensch, Paulus van Dorsten and Martijn.

projects.title: Respect!, exhibition design
projects.excerpt: A sensor-driven light design for Respect!, where each work stays dark until someone comes close enough to look at it.
projects.description:
Respect! Perspectieven in de hedendaagse kunst ran at Museum De Voorde in Zoetermeer from 5 February to 2 October 2022. The museum has since closed. Eighteen Dutch artists worked to the theme of respect, among them Rob Sweere, Frode Bolhuis, Marjolijn Mandersloot, Tobias Becker Hoff and spoken word artist Amara van der Elst.
I made the exhibition and light design. Every work had its own sensor: the light came up as a visitor approached and went out again when they left, so the room was only ever lit where somebody was actually looking.
> The theme was respect, so the light had to be asked for rather than given. Nothing is lit until you walk up to it, and it goes dark again behind you. Paying attention is what switches the work on.
> It also means the room reads the crowd. On a busy afternoon the whole space is alive; late in the day a single visitor moves through it as one travelling pool of light.
projects.credits: Exhibition design, light design and sensor system: Jaco Schilp. Motion sensors driving DMX, one per work. Respect! Perspectieven in de hedendaagse kunst, Museum De Voorde, Zoetermeer, since closed, 5 February to 2 October 2022, with eighteen Dutch artists.

projects.title: Circuitry (Live A/V)
projects.role: A/V live performance & visuals (with Skander Jaïbi & Skander Ben Yahia)
projects.excerpt: A live audiovisual performance with Skander Jaïbi, built on modular synthesis and real-time 3D visuals, premiered at Modulation / Etmaal Festival.
projects.description:
> Circuitry is a live audiovisual performance created with Skander Jaïbi and Skander Ben Yahia, built around modular synthesis and real-time 3D visuals. Sound and image are wired together: the music drives the visuals and the visuals feed back into the performance, an evolving circuit of light and electronics.
It premiered for Modulation, the modular-synthesizer series run by Sonar Traffic at Kytopia in Utrecht, and at Etmaal, the 24-hour festival curated by Colin Benders.
projects.credits: A/V live performance: Jaco Schilp, Skander Jaïbi & Skander Ben Yahia (sound & music). Premiered for Modulation (Sonar Traffic) at Etmaal Festival, curated by Colin Benders. Photography: Paulus van Dorsten. Recording: Sonar Traffic.

projects.title: Orbit Festival
projects.excerpt: Light design for all stages of Orbit Festival.
projects.description:
I have been part of Orbit Festival for five editions, creating the light design for all stages, with light as the connective tissue between music, architecture and crowd, operated live to shape the energy of each space as the night unfolded.
> Towering luminous totems, glowing canopies and beams cut through the haze of the festival's wooded grounds.
projects.credits: Production: ESWA licht en geluid. Photography: TB.

projects.title: Human Nature for Kinki × L'Oréal
projects.role: Visual content & projection mapping (with Cris Mollee)
projects.excerpt: “Human Nature”, a Kinki Kappers show for L'Oréal Pro: 3D-scanned models, four chapters, and projection-mapped digital worlds.
projects.description:
> Human Nature is a show created by Kinki Kappers for L'Oréal Pro, telling a story about the relationship between our human nature and the Metaverse: the light and darkness in us all as we build the digital world.
The show is built on 3D scans of the catwalk models, processed in TouchDesigner into four chapters, each with its own digital scenery and timecode-automated light. I created the visual content and projection mapping together with Cris Mollee (LiGHT-UP Collective), wrapping the runway and stage in shifting digital landscapes for models, dancers and aerial performers.
projects.credits: A Kinki Kappers show for L'Oréal Pro, “Human Nature”. Art direction: Casper. Projection mapping & content: Jaco Schilp & Cris Mollee (LiGHT-UP Collective). Choreography: Virgil Moreno & Meyline. Music: The Shirley Temple. Photography: Fabrice Debatty.

projects.title: 50 jaar Van Gogh Museum
projects.excerpt: An LED wall in the museum's entrance hall for its fiftieth birthday night, made with Skander Jaïbi and Cris Mollee from the digital files of the full collection.
projects.description:
An evening marking the museum's fiftieth birthday, from 19:00 to 23:30, with music, dance, film and storytelling through the building.
I made the visuals for the large LED wall in the entrance hall, working from the museum's digital files of the full Van Gogh collection. Every painting was rebuilt in TouchDesigner and ran on the wall through the evening as the crowd gathered.
> Working from the museum's own scans means starting where the paintings already are: flat, lit evenly, measured. Blown up to the height of the hall and moving, they stop being reproductions and become something the room happens inside of.
> The night was built around the same question as the wall: after fifty years, what does the next fifty look like, and what is a museum for.
projects.credits: Visuals: Jaco Schilp. Built in TouchDesigner from the museum's digital files of the full Van Gogh collection, shown on a large LED wall in the entrance hall. Part of the fiftieth birthday programme at the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam, 2023, with Nnelg, Rens, Jaïr & Ome Uncle, ISH Dance Collectief, storytelling collective Mezrab, a film programme with Lab 111, and DJ sets by Fatima Ferrari, Donn Stone and DJ Dey.Rey.

projects.title: BYOB Utrecht Citytour
projects.excerpt: BYOB's tenth anniversary: a one-night city tour of projections across nine pop-up galleries in Utrecht.
projects.description:
Bring Your Own Beamer 2020. For BYOB's tenth anniversary we turned the city of Utrecht into a one-night tour of projections, installations and performances across nine pop-up public galleries, on 26 September 2020. The edition ran as part of NFF interactive, the Dutch Film Festival programme for trans-medial and interactive work, and because of the covid measures the whole thing moved into the public space: an evening walk through the city, from location to location.
> BYOB is a non-hierarchical, open-call format: participants aren't curated but facilitated, choosing where and how to show their work. Made possible by more than 50 participants and over 1,000 visitors, all within the strict COVID-19 regulations of the time.
projects.credits: Organised by Jaco Schilp. Part of NFF interactive at the Nederlands Film Festival, Utrecht, 2020.

projects.title: Uncloud 2019
projects.excerpt: The third edition of the Uncloud festival at EKKO, Utrecht.
projects.description: The third edition of the Uncloud festival at EKKO, Utrecht. Line-up included Deena Abdelwahed, Zoë McPherson, Bendik Giske, Renick Bell, GNOD (R&D), Mark IJzerman, Modulation and Stranded FM.
projects.credits: A project by Uncloud, curated by Jaco Schilp & Skander Jaïbi.

projects.title: Orbit Interactive Installation
projects.excerpt: An interactive installation that reimagines drone-tracking AI as a tool for play and connection.
projects.description:
A project especially close to me: an interactive installation commissioned by Orbit Festival, alongside the light design for all stages.
> Built in TouchDesigner and guided by an AI model once developed for military drones to track bodies and objects, the work seeks to shift perspective, to reimagine technology born from conflict as a tool for connection and play. As an artist, I feel it is important to explore how these systems can transform when placed in a different light.
projects.credits: Concept, design and TouchDesigner: Jaco Schilp. Commissioned by Orbit Festival, 2025. Film: Guillaume Versteeg.

projects.title: Soenda Presents
projects.excerpt: Light design for the dance floor, capturing the energy and impression of light in motion.
projects.description: Light design and atmosphere for Soenda Presents. These moments capture the energy and impression of the lights on the dance floor, built and operated live for the night.
projects.credits: Light & design: Jaco Schilp. Photos: Elske Nissen. Production: ESWA licht en geluid. With Lammer at Soenda.

projects.title: Buy or Burn: 11.1 Rotterdam
projects.excerpt: "Between Physical and Digital: An Abstract Interpretation of Rotterdam." Laser-cut point-cloud data of the city.
projects.description:
Presented at Brutus, Rotterdam, with No Es Una Galería. This artwork exists at the intersection of the physical and digital, where technology and human intuition merge to create a new visual language.
> The creation began with the urban landscape of Rotterdam, captured through 3D scanning. These scans, transformed into point-cloud data, serve as the foundation for an artistic reinterpretation of the city. A laser cutter, acting as both tool and an agent of chance, introduces a layer of unpredictability, ensuring the result is shaped not only by precision but also by material resistance and machine limitations. This interplay of control and randomness mirrors the tension between order and chaos within the city itself.
projects.credits: Black acrylic, LED panel, black aluminium frame. 120 × 30 cm. 3D-scanned point-cloud data (LAS), TouchDesigner.

projects.title: No Art Festival: Synergy
projects.excerpt: A large-scale open-air exhibition of 10 installations at the NDSM werf, Amsterdam.
projects.description:
For the first edition of No Art Festival, I curated my first large-scale open-air exhibition at the NDSM werf in Amsterdam. The exhibition brought together 10 large-scale art installations in collaboration with music label No Art, with more than fifteen young contemporary visual artists and collectives from Amsterdam-North and surroundings.

The centrepiece was Boris Acket's WAAIWERK, 60 by 10 metres, an interactive work of sound and light controlled by the wind.
projects.credits: Curated by Jaco Schilp. In collaboration with No Art.

projects.title: Circle of Live at MUTEK Mexico
projects.excerpt: An immersive real-time visual environment for the four-hour Circle of Live session at MUTEK Mexico 2025.
projects.description:
For the four-hour Circle of Live session at MUTEK MX 21 in October 2025, I made the real-time visuals and light environment in Hall A of Maravilla Studios, Mexico City, with multimedia artist and lighting designer Pavel Zmuchila and choreographer Alejandra Metztli.
The images ran in TouchDesigner off my own LiDAR scans of the city, captured over a day of cycling an Ecobici with cameras strapped to it, along Reforma and through Roma and Chapultepec. Four more LiDAR scanners stood around the venue during the show, so the pre-recorded city and the live room fed the same system. Pavel drove the light from a GrandMA desk blended with TouchDesigner bitmaps for the pixel fixtures, everything merged into one DMX output.
> Eight dancer platforms circled the musicians, and Metztli's Butoh choreography followed natural elements and the Fibonacci spiral. The rule we set ourselves was never to overload the senses: when the dancers led, the visuals softened; when the music rose, the light took the room.
> Working from scanned data means the city is already in the machine before the night starts. What the evening decides is which parts of it come back, and from an angle no camera could have stood in.
projects.credits: Real-time visuals and LiDAR: Jaco Schilp / Studio Schilp. Light: Pavel Zmuchila. Choreography: Alejandra Metztli, with eight dancers. Programmed with Damián Romero. Circle of Live: Sebastian Mullaert, Pantha du Prince and Leafar Legov. Founded by Sebastian Mullaert. MUTEK MX 21 Nocturne, Hall A, Maravilla Studios, Mexico City, 10 October 2025. Photos: Diego Figueroa, Leo Luna and David Barajas.

insight.title: Planning and instinct
insight.intro: MUTEK MX spoke to the three of us about how the night in Hall A was built: Pavel Zmuchila on light, Alejandra Metztli on choreography, and me on the real-time images.

a.text: That idea immediately aligned with what MUTEK MX was looking for: something that balanced the digital with the physical.

qa.q: How did Circle of Live's improvisation shape the work?

a.text: This helped us respond intuitively to what was happening on stage. Everyone reacted live, always checking if there was room to add something or if it was better to hold back.

qa.q: What were you after with the circular design?

a.text: It was important to think about four elements: the physical sensation of the space, the lighting, the visuals, and the choreography.

qa.q: How do you prepare for operating it live?

a.text: The process was a mix of planning and instinct. The three of us had long conversations about how the night might unfold.

qa.q: What did Maravilla Studios give you?

a.text: Its scale allowed the circular design and 360-degree experience to truly feel at home.
One of the biggest challenges was making sure we didn't overwhelm people.
I worked with TouchDesigner to create real-time images using data from LiDAR scans of Mexico.

projects.title: Circle of Live at Cervantino
projects.location: Main stage, Festival Internacional Cervantino, Guanajuato
projects.excerpt: The second Mexican Circle of Live night, presented with MUTEK MX at the Festival Internacional Cervantino.
projects.description:
The second Mexican Circle of Live night, presented as MUTEK MX x Festival Internacional Cervantino on 12 October 2025, two days after the Nocturne session in Mexico City. Same collaboration, different room, this time the festival's main stage, outdoors in Guanajuato: real-time visuals and light from me, choreography by Alejandra Metztli.
> A set built for one venue has to be rebuilt for the next, and what survives the move is the part that was really the work. In Mexico City the audience circled the musicians. Here it was an outdoor main stage with a crowd in front of it, so the point clouds had to hold a whole square instead of a room.
projects.credits: Real-time visuals and light: Jaco Schilp / Studio Schilp. Choreography: Alejandra Metztli. Circle of Live: Sebastian Mullaert, Pantha du Prince and Leafar Legov. MUTEK MX x Festival Internacional Cervantino, main stage, Guanajuato, 12 October 2025.

projects.title: Archive Mirror
projects.location: Treehouse NDSM, Amsterdam · Pieterskerk, Leiden · Art Week Mexico City
projects.excerpt: An interactive installation with painter Santiago Pani, where a camera and an AI model trained on his archive turn visitors into evolving portraits.
projects.description:
Archive Mirror is an interactive installation by Jaco Schilp and Santiago Pani that explores the meeting point between traditional painting and digital technology. A live camera captures participants, while a custom-trained AI model built on an archive of Pani's abstract portraits translates their presence into evolving visual compositions.
> As visitors stand before the system, they become both subject and collaborator, triggering a real-time feedback loop between body, camera, and algorithm. The work reflects Pani's exploration of the human figure as fragmented memory, while extending it into a dynamic, generative space shaped by Schilp's digital practice.
> By training the AI on past works, the installation questions authorship, originality, and control. Rather than replacing the artist, the system acts as an unpredictable partner, revealing new forms that exist between intention and autonomy, where the archive continuously meets the present.
projects.credits: An installation by Jaco Schilp and Santiago Pani. Painting and archive: Santiago Pani. Camera system, AI model and real-time visuals: Jaco Schilp. Shown in Two Suns At Once at Treehouse NDSM, Amsterdam, 2026, co-curated by Vico Persson and supported by AFK; in the Pieterskerk, Leiden, 2025; and in Todo pasa at Público, Mexico City, during Art Week Mexico City 2026, presented with Lagom Studio Galería. Documentary: Guillaume Versteeg.

projects.title: Points of Light
projects.excerpt: 10 years of research, 14 million data points, 14 laser projectors, turning the Grote Kerk into a real-time light environment.
projects.description:
> Ten years of research. 14 million data points. 14 laser projectors.
What started a decade ago as a research project between Jaco Schilp and Jan Willem Campmans has finally pushed through the technical ceiling, turning the historic Grote Kerk in Den Haag into a real-time data environment. Using TouchDesigner's POP operators, the work runs a full LiDAR 3D scan of the cathedral, 14 million particles calibrated in real time. No pre-renders, no loops: raw architecture translated into light.
Visitors experience the intersection of history and high-performance code. Presented in January 2026 in 15-minute projections, free entry.
projects.credits: Video animations & custom calibration: Studio Schilp (TouchDesigner). Digital light animations: Sem Schreuder (Unreal Engine). Sound: Alejandra Metztli. Projectors sponsored by Epson. Hosted at Grote Kerk Den Haag / the Greanery. Film: Jokko Voogt.

projects.title: Lely's Droom
projects.role: 3D scan, point cloud projection, projection mapping & show control
projects.excerpt: An immersive experience in the Oosterlanderkerk built around rediscovered recordings of Cornelis Lely, made exactly a hundred years earlier.
projects.description:
Lely's Droom is a fifteen minute immersive experience in the Oosterlanderkerk in Oosterland on Wieringen, made by LiGHT-UP Collective, Jan Willem Campmans and Jaco Schilp for Erfgoedspektakel and shown through May 2025, with Tristan Gieler on the content. The church stands a short distance from the Afsluitdijk, which is the subject of the piece.
It starts from rediscovered sound recordings that Cornelis Lely made in May 1925, exactly a hundred years before the piece was shown. He speaks to whoever is still interested in his dream a century later, appearing in the church as a life size animated figure, voiced by Rik Rikken. Projection and light carry his story: the first plans from 1848, the years of rejection, the flood of January 1916 that killed twenty one people on land and thirty two more at sea, the Zuiderzeewet of 1918, the Amsteldiepdijk built to learn on, the Wieringen boulder clay that finally held, and the Afsluitdijk itself.
Lely died at his desk in January 1929 and never saw the work finished.
I made a full 3D scan of the church and projected it back onto its own geometry with my point cloud system in TouchDesigner, driving the points with displacement so the building itself starts to move like water. Between the shows the space held an idle state running on a soundscape I made for it.
> Scanning the church and projecting it back onto itself means the building is both the screen and the subject. Push displacement into those points and the stone begins to move like water, which is the whole argument of the piece in one gesture: the land here is only ever borrowed from the sea.
> Water is always moving, so waterworks are never finished. That is Lely's own line, and it is the reason the piece is addressed forward rather than back: he is not being commemorated, he is asking what we are doing with the problem now.
projects.credits: A LiGHT-UP Collective production, Jaco Schilp and Jan Willem Campmans, for Erfgoedspektakel at the Oosterlanderkerk, Oosterland, Wieringen, 2025. Voice of Cornelis Lely: Rik Rikken. 3D scan of the church, point cloud projection onto its own geometry, particle effects, simulated water and the idle state soundscape: Jaco Schilp. Point cloud system built in TouchDesigner, water animated in Cinema 4D with RealFlow. Projection mapping and show control: Jaco Schilp and Merijn Meijers. Unreal Engine support for the life size animated figure of Lely: Sem Schreuder. Life size animated 3D character of Cornelis Lely, motion graphics, animation, editing and archival research in the Dutch national archives: Tristan Gieler, who also composed and produced the original score. Film: Jokko Voogt. Initiated by BOEi, with Gemeente Hollands Kroon, Culturele Kring Wieringen and the VriendenLoterij.

projects.title: Schiedam 750
projects.excerpt: Real-time generative video mapping on the Alevitisch Cultureel Centrum for Schiedam's 750th anniversary.
projects.description: For Schiedam's 750th anniversary I created a custom video mapping on the Alevitisch Cultureel Centrum. Using the building's own geometry, I designed a real-time TouchDesigner patch to bring the facade to life, projected with a 30,000-lumen Epson laser projector and reflected in the water below.
projects.credits: Produced and commissioned by LightUp Collective.

projects.title: Mexico City Point Clouds
projects.excerpt: Scanning Mexico City myself, and finding out what the buildings become once they are only measurement and light.
projects.description:
Ongoing research in Mexico City, built from my own LiDAR scans rather than from open aerial data. I walk the buildings and scan them at close range, so the cloud carries the position I stood in, what the scanner could see from there and what it could not.
Landmarks such as the Palacio de Bellas Artes come back as millions of points, dense where I stayed and thin where I passed.
> This one is research, not an edition series. Scanning a city yourself is slower and more partial than taking the data from the air, and that partiality is the point: what you get is not the building, it is the record of an encounter with it.
projects.credits: Own LiDAR scans, point cloud work and rendering: Jaco Schilp. Mexico City.

projects.title: 3FM Awards
projects.excerpt: The first sensor-driven holographic visuals on Dutch TV, with a pepper-scrim cube responding live to the performance.
projects.description:
The first-ever sensor-driven visuals on Dutch television. For the 3FM Awards I created the projections, a holographic installation and the live visuals. An open cube of pepper scrim produced holographic effects, and sensor-driven technology made the imagery respond in real time to the movements of DI-RECT's singer during their live performance.

Built with a combination of Resolume, TouchDesigner, Unreal Engine, Kinect and point-cloud satellite data, it offered a new way to experience live music on television.
projects.credits: In collaboration with LiGHT-UP Collective.

projects.title: Reports from Other Continents
projects.excerpt: A public media installation for Le Guess Who? 2021, bringing thirty global reports to the streets of Utrecht.
projects.description: For Le Guess Who? 2021, together with Roel Weerdenburg, I created a public media installation presenting thirty reports from all over the world to the shopping public of the city of Utrecht.
projects.credits: With Roel Weerdenburg. Le Guess Who? 2021.

projects.title: The Greenery, Westergas
projects.excerpt: An immersive 360° dining experience, with ingredients filmed in macro and projected across 400 m² of canvas.
projects.description:
An immersive 360 degree dining experience. For a pop-up restaurant in the Gashouder at the Westergasfabriek in Amsterdam, the whole room was video mapped and transformed completely with each course, with custom content for every dish. Ingredients were filmed with a high-speed macro camera and projected across a 400 square metre wrap-around canvas.
A box projection driven by eight 20,000 lumen projectors in collaboration with Beamsystems, running on custom mediaservers, with real-time 3D content generated in Unreal Engine, Blender and TouchDesigner.
> Dinner became somewhere to be rather than something to look at. As each plate arrived the room went with it, so the guests were eating inside the ingredient.
projects.credits: In co-creation with LiGHT-UP Collective. Projection in collaboration with Beamsystems, eight 20,000 lumen projectors. Sponsored by Panasonic. Photos: Dennis Bouman.

projects.title: Sonaural
projects.excerpt: An immersive site-specific AV performance with Skander Jaïbi at WORM, Rotterdam, moving from drone to brutalist intensity.
projects.description: An immersive, site-specific audiovisual performance with Skander Jaïbi, presented at WORM in Rotterdam as part of Sonaural (2020). Combining modular synthesizers, projectors, TouchDesigner, local satellite data and 3D scanning, the piece begins as a slow drone and builds into a brutalist, intense crescendo of sound and light.
projects.credits: With Skander Jaïbi. Presented at Sonaural, WORM, Rotterdam, 2020.

projects.title: HKU Graduation Bonanza
projects.excerpt: Graduation work by more than 60 HKU students projected across Utrecht, after covid cancelled their exhibition.
projects.description:
Covid restrictions meant the HKU in Utrecht could not hold a physical graduation exhibition, so we proposed projecting the work through the city instead. What started as a gesture towards the media students was picked up by every faculty, and more than 60 students submitted work. We took it on a projection tour of the public space.
> A graduation show is a threshold, and that year it had nowhere to happen. Putting the work on the walls of the city gave it an audience that had not come to see art, which is a harder and better audience to have.
projects.credits: A LiGHT-UP Collective project with the HKU, University of the Arts Utrecht. Graduation work by more than 60 HKU students, projected in the public space of Utrecht, 2020.

projects.title: Universum 1.2
projects.excerpt: An interactive light sculpture: an abstract planet that answers to how visitors move through the room.
projects.description:
Universum 1.2 is an interactive light sculpture made with Skander Jaïbi for Museum van Geluid.
Lasers in the space were triggered by where people stood. Those triggers drove the soundscape, and the soundscape triggered the visuals, so a visitor's movement travelled through sound before it ever arrived as light. The sphere hung from an electromotor and turned continuously, with the mapping built to stay locked to the shape as it moved.
> An abstract planet, small enough to stand beside. Where you put yourself in the room changes how it behaves, so nobody meets quite the same planet, and nobody has it to themselves.
> It opens a space between two worlds, the digital abstract one and the physical analogue one we live in. Holding them together makes a new micro universe where the two become one.
> The work is part of an ongoing research into making the digital physically tangible, looking for a digital reality that can be shared with everyone.
projects.credits: Jaco Schilp: 3D sculpture and video mapping. Skander Jaïbi: interactive soundscape. Laser sensors trigger the soundscape, the soundscape triggers the visuals. Sphere mounted on a rotating electromotor, with the mapping tracking the turning shape. Presented at Museum van Geluid, 2018.

projects.title: Stedelijk Museum Schiedam
projects.excerpt: A month of projections on the Schiedam municipal office, made with the Stedelijk Museum Schiedam.
projects.description:
Together with the Stedelijk Museum Schiedam we projected on the municipal office of Schiedam for over a month, night after night, with personal and artistic content.
> A city building is not usually somewhere people look. For a month it was, and what appeared on it belonged to the people walking past rather than to the institution behind the windows.
projects.credits: Projection: LiGHT-UP Collective in collaboration with the Stedelijk Museum Schiedam, on the Schiedam stadskantoor, 2021. Edit: Vincent van den Brink.

projects.title: Caravaggio opening, Centraal Museum
projects.excerpt: Projection work for the opening night of the Caravaggio exhibition at the Centraal Museum in Utrecht.
projects.description:
For the opening of the Caravaggio exhibition at the Centraal Museum in Utrecht, in December 2018, I made the projection mapping and the content.
> Caravaggio built his paintings out of light falling into darkness, so the projections worked the same way: the museum lit only where the light chose to land, and the rest of the room left to the dark.
projects.credits: Projection mapping & content: Jaco Schilp, with LiGHT-UP Collective. Centraal Museum, Utrecht, December 2018. Camera: Jokko Voogt. Edit: Ajehna Rustveld.

projects.title: Kunsthal Rotterdam, Museumnacht
projects.excerpt: My first large outdoor projection mapping: the facade of the Kunsthal Rotterdam for Museumnacht 2017.
projects.description:
For Museumnacht 2017 Jan Willem Campmans and I mapped the facade of the Kunsthal Rotterdam. It was my first large outdoor projection mapping project, and the start of the building-scale work that followed.
> The Kunsthal's facade is already a composition of planes and materials, so the mapping followed the building rather than covering it, letting content run along its own lines and edges until the architecture read as something built out of light.
projects.credits: Projection mapping: Jaco Schilp and Jan Willem Campmans, with LiGHT-UP Collective. Presented during Museumnacht at the Kunsthal Rotterdam, 2017.

projects.title: NCCA Nizhny Novgorod, Museum Night
projects.location: National Centre for Contemporary Arts, Nizhny Novgorod
projects.excerpt: Museum Night at the NCCA in Nizhny Novgorod: light-drawing workshops by day, live performances with local musicians, and the facade mapped at night for over 30,000 visitors.
projects.description:
For Museum Night 2019 the whole LiGHT-UP team of that moment travelled to Nizhny Novgorod, Russia: Tim Walther, Lisa Derksen Castillo, Jan Willem Campmans and me.
We began with a light-drawing workshop for children, drawing with light on PlayStation uDraw tablets running Happytron, LiGHT-UP's own application for drawing with projected light.
Then came the performances. I played live first indoors, together with local musicians from Nizhny, and at night we moved the projectors outside and mapped the facade of the museum for more than 30,000 visitors.
The content was everything I had brought with me, pre-rendered, mixed with 3D animations of the building that we modelled on the spot in Cinema 4D and ran through Resolume effects.
> Working on an unfamiliar building in an unfamiliar city meant reading the architecture from scratch, in a few days, and finding what the facade wanted to do with light before the night began.
projects.credits: LiGHT-UP Collective: Tim Walther, Lisa Derksen Castillo, Jan Willem Campmans and Jaco Schilp. Light-drawing workshops on PlayStation uDraw tablets running Happytron, LiGHT-UP's light-drawing application, conceived by Jan Willem Campmans and developed with Tim Walther. Building animations in Cinema 4D, played live in Resolume. Live performance with musicians from Nizhny Novgorod. Hosted by the NCCA, Nizhny Novgorod, Museum Night 2019. With thanks to Anna Gorokhovskaya, Aeger Smoothie, Anna Gor, Anna Kostyan, Xenia Anoufrieva, technician Alexander, and the amazing help of Polina Ashina.
